chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said:

I mentioned to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) the khuras (land tax) and what the people of his household practiced, so he said: 'The tenth and half of the tenth is upon whoever embraces Islam voluntarily, if his land is left in his hand; the tenth and half of the tenth are taken from him regarding what he cultivates of it, and what he does not cultivate of it, the governor takes it and leases it to whoever cultivates it, and it belongs to the Muslims. And there is no tax on what is less than five awsiq. And what is conquered by the sword, that belongs to the Imam, who leases it as he sees fit, as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did with Khaybar; he leased its land and its palm trees, while the people said that leasing the land and palm trees is not suitable if the white (fertile land) is more than the black (less fertile). And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) leased Khaybar — and upon them, in their shares, is the tenth and half of the tenth.'

key_terms.خَمْسَةُ أَوْسَاقٍ: Five awsiq (a unit of measurement for grain)
key_terms.خَيْبَرَ: Khaybar (a region known for its fertile land and palm trees)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on land tax (khuras) for new converts and conquered lands according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) delineates the fiscal jurisprudence of land tax (kharaj), distinguishing between voluntary converts who pay a 15% levy on cultivated land and the state's management of uncultivated plots. He explicitly validates the practice of leasing (qibalah) conquered lands, citing the Prophet’s precedent at Khaybar to affirm the Imam’s authority to determine lease terms, a key concept in Shia administrative law. This narration underscores the continuity of Prophetic economic practices under the guidance of the Ahl al-Bayt.
